headline: Good morning — Wall Street's AI-led rout dragged the ASX lower, and department store David Jones has collapsed into administration.

highlights.label: Wall Street rout
highlights.text: The Nasdaq fell about 5.5% and the S&P 500 about 4.4% on an AI and chip stock sell-off.

highlights.label: David Jones collapse
highlights.text: The 188-year-old retailer entered voluntary administration and receivership after talks with landlords broke down; stores keep trading for now.

highlights.label: ASX slides
highlights.text: The ASX 200 opened about 1.1% lower and the Australian dollar dropped to roughly 69 US cents.

tip.title: Do a short strength set before your shower
tip.body: Two or three rounds of bodyweight squats and wall or incline push-ups take under five minutes and need no equipment. Attaching the habit to something you already do makes it easier to repeat, and regular strength work supports muscle, bone and mood.

quote.text: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
quote.author: Will Durant

items.title: Adobe puts its CX Enterprise Coworker inside major AI assistants
items.summary: Adobe made its CX Enterprise Coworker available inside ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot and Databricks Genie on 4 November, with more platforms listed as coming soon. No adoption figures or pricing were disclosed, so the commercial impact is unclear.

items.title: HubSpot reports Q3 2026 results
items.summary: HubSpot held its third-quarter earnings call on 4 November; a secondary roundup cites revenue of about US$947.6 million, up 17%. Figures are from a secondary source and should be checked against HubSpot's release.

items.title: HubSpot starts enforcing marketplace platform version requirements
items.summary: HubSpot began enforcing platform version requirements for marketplace apps from 2 November. Teams with connected apps should check their integrations still comply.

items.title: HubSpot phasing out Design Manager serverless functions
items.summary: HubSpot is retiring Design Manager serverless functions and Node.js 20, with existing functions editable until 17 November 2026. Developers need to migrate before then.

items.title: Adobe Journey Optimizer adds token resolution for AEM content fragments
items.summary: Adobe Journey Optimizer added limited-availability support for resolving personalisation tokens inside Experience Manager Content Fragments. It should reduce workarounds when personalising managed content.

items.title: Salesforce completes acquisition of Loops
items.summary: An editor's note says the Loops deal closed on 2 November 2026. Loops is an AI analytics platform that Salesforce plans to fold into Tableau.

items.title: Dreamforce 2026 announcements roundup
items.summary: The recap says Hyperforce on Google Cloud is slated for general availability in North America in November 2026, and the Hunter agent is expected to reach general availability the same month. Dates are from a third-party recap.

items.title: Salesforce's agreed Braze acquisition raises questions for email platforms
items.summary: Analysis of Salesforce's deal to buy Braze at US$47.50 a share, about US$5.66 billion, with closing expected in fiscal 2028. The commentary looks at the effect on email and engagement platforms. The deal coverage is about two weeks old.

sfstatus.statusNote: Salesforce Trust could not be checked directly; a third-party tracker showed no active incidents, with the latest incident resolved on 31 October.

items.title: David Jones collapses into voluntary administration
items.summary: The department store entered administration and receivership after talks with its landlord Westfield broke down, with reports of about 6,000 jobs at risk. Stores and online sales continue while the receivers review the business.

items.title: What David Jones shoppers should know about gift cards
items.summary: An explainer on consumer rights as the retailer failed, with advocates arguing gift card funds should be protected. It matters for customers holding cards or pending orders.

items.title: ASX falls sharply as US tech stocks plunge
items.summary: The local share market dropped at the open after the Wall Street AI sell-off, with the tech sector hit hardest. Investors are weighing US midterm fallout and the RBA's recent rate decision.

items.title: Debate over India's Muslims after jailed scholar case
items.summary: A jailed scholar's case has prompted debate on whether India's democracy has failed its Muslims. Listed 5 November; details not independently confirmed here.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall on India's east coast
items.summary: The cyclone struck the eastern coast on 3 November. Older than 48 hours.

items.title: Assam evictions displace thousands
items.summary: Thousands were reported displaced as homes were bulldozed in Assam, per a 3 November report. Older than 48 hours.

items.title: Sensex surges over 2,000 points on sixth straight gain
items.summary: The Sensex reportedly rose 2.60% to 79,310.01 and the Nifty closed at 24,536.60 ahead of Dhanteras. Date and figures come from a single secondary source.

items.title: Protest over removals from voter rolls in New Delhi
items.summary: Protesters on 1 November carried a one-kilometre banner listing people removed from voter rolls. Older than 48 hours.

items.title: Andhra Pradesh votes in MPTC and ZPTC local elections
items.summary: Voting opened on Thursday across 31,460 polling centres under heavy security. Polling was postponed in some mandals of Eluru and East Godavari because of heavy rain.

items.title: Early turnout in NTR and Krishna districts
items.summary: Turnout stood above 14% in NTR district and 15% in Krishna district by morning. Final turnout figures were not yet available.

items.title: Naidu reviews Amaravati capital construction
items.summary: The chief minister held a high-level review of capital works in Amaravati. This is an April 2026 story used as background because nothing newer was found.

items.title: Nasdaq has its worst day in 18 months as AI trade unravels
items.summary: The Nasdaq suffered its sharpest fall in about 18 months as investors dumped AI and chip names. The sell-off followed a strong rally on 4 November.

items.title: Nvidia and AMD slump on chip sell-off
items.summary: Nvidia fell about 9% and AMD about 17% as investors cut semiconductor exposure after the Democratic midterm sweep. Election uncertainty is cited as a driver.

items.title: Amazon shares slide as technology sell-off erases gains
items.summary: Amazon fell as early gains vanished in the broad tech sell-off. It shows the weakness reached beyond chipmakers.

items.title: AI stocks wipeout sends Wall Street reeling
items.summary: AI-related stocks sank while many world shares had gained after the US midterms. Closing figures are from CNBC and Motley Fool reports.

items.title: ASX opens sharply lower after Wall Street AI rout
items.summary: The ASX 200 opened about 1.1% lower, with technology down roughly 1.3%. Figures are from the open and will move through the session.

items.title: Australian shares set to fall after US AI rout
items.summary: Futures pointed to a fall of about 0.5% before the open. The briefing also reports board unease over how the RBA signalled its rate rise.

items.title: Aussie dollar plunges amid US stock sell-off
items.summary: The Australian dollar fell about 1% to near 69 US cents on risk aversion. The RBA's split decision to lift the cash rate on 3 November also weighed.

items.title: ASX preview: Macquarie half-year result in focus
items.summary: Macquarie Group's first-half results are due, with shares expected to fall and oil surging. Results could swing the financials.

items.title: Home values fall 1.2% in October
items.summary: Cotality's index fell 1.2% in October, leaving values 6.7% below the March 2026 peak but 3.7% above a year earlier. Sydney is about 8.6% off its peak and Melbourne about 7.2%.

items.title: CBA braces for record housing downturn
items.summary: CBA expects a deep price correction and rising rental yields toward 4.75% by late 2027. The forecast is the bank's projection, not a certainty.

items.title: RBA rate hike hits the auction market
items.summary: Auction clearance rates dropped after the RBA lifted rates. Older than 48 hours; newer clearance data was not found.

items.title: Auction clearance rate sinks to three-month low
items.summary: The preliminary clearance rate fell to 48.2%, with unsold stock up more than 20% on a year earlier. Dated 5 October, used for background.
